findings.title: Route-table detector reports unrelated slash-keyed tuples as served endpoints
findings.what: The detector scans the entire server source for every array pair shaped like `['/path', identifier]`. It does not verify that the pair is inside a route Map or that the Map is subsequently queried with `pathname`. Consequently, an unrelated tuple such as `const metadata = [['/api/example', handler]]` is classified as a served endpoint, making the freshness result non-reproducible from actual dispatch behavior. The negative test covers only non-slash string pairs and identifier-keyed pairs, so it cannot expose this ambiguity.
findings.fix: Restrict extraction to entries inside a recognized route-map declaration whose identifier is demonstrably queried with `.get(pathname)`, preferably using a syntax-aware parser; add a regression fixture containing an unrelated `['/api/not-a-route', handler]` tuple.
findings.acceptance: A regression test proves that an unrelated slash-leading string/identifier tuple produces no served route, while an entry in a Map that is queried with `.get(pathname)` is still collected and drift detection continues to flag undocumented real table routes.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read of scripts/check-openapi-freshness.mjs:65-98 confirmed that the only route-table qualification is the tuple regex at line 95, with no surrounding Map or `.get(pathname)` check. Re-read of scripts/check-openapi-freshness.test.mjs:39-75 confirmed the positive fixture includes both contextual signals but the negative fixture never exercises the ambiguous slash-string/identifier shape.
